title: Roll Dispenser
description: A roll dispenser born from curiosity about everyday objects that feel forgotten as technology moves on. The goal was to streamline the whole act of using it while cutting waste, and to make something that fits a modern home. It isn't limited to the kitchen or restroom: it adjusts to anything that comes on a roll, and taken further it could do away with the cardboard core altogether.

brief.label: Objective
brief.text: Streamline using the object, reduce waste and make it more sustainable, while fitting modern homes.

brief.label: Mounting
brief.text: Simple enough to screw-mount, or to pressure-fit through slots in a cabinet thanks to the plastic's flexibility.

brief.label: Packaging
brief.text: None. The arms let it hang on store shelves, and it's durable enough to ship with minimal support, saving cost and material.

brief.label: Material
brief.text: Bio-on PHA bioplastic: strong, 100% biodegradable and fully natural, water-resistant, with a porous surface that takes paint.

brief.label: Key features
brief.text: Operational simplicity. Sustainable packaging and make-up. Form flexibility.

brief.label: Process
brief.text: Sketch ideation, then paper and cardboard prototypes to test the fold, then kitchen and restroom versions in a final visualization.

study_intro: Reduction as the design language: one folded form does the whole job.

study.label: Form
study.text: A single folded sheet, where one bend makes the arm and another the cradle, so the roll and the next sheet are always presented.

study.label: Gesture
study.text: Prototyped in paper and card, so the object keeps the honesty of a fold: nothing is added that the material couldn't do on its own.

study.label: Color
study.text: Coral red and deep green over a pale ground: bright enough to be a deliberate object on the wall, not hidden hardware.

study.label: Flexibility
study.text: The same profile reads as a kitchen piece or a restroom piece, and adapts to anything that comes on a roll.
